purpose: The infrastructure band of a marketing page: a tall framed panel with the world network map drawn behind a small start-aligned title, a claims eyebrow and a row of claim chips, closed by a floor of client outcomes (a quote with its highlights and, when given, the client's mark), benefits (a topic each) or stats (headline figures). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'network-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `network-map`, `section-title`, `card-grid`, `quote`, `feature-item` and `stats`. `variant` picks the floor only: `outcomes` renders the quotes on one column per entry — two at least, four at most; `benefits` renders the topics on up to three columns, balanced so every row is full; `stats` renders the figures as a `stats` row. The band above is the same.
useWhen: To state the network's reach with figures and back it with client results, product benefits or headline figures.
avoidWhen: For figures alone, without the map band → use `stats-section`.
For a logo wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-section`.
related: `network-map` — the animated map behind the copy.
`quote` / `feature-item` — the cell types of the `outcomes` and `benefits` floors.
bestPractices: Four short `claims`; they are chips, not sentences. Give a claim as `{ label, mobile: false }` to keep it to the medium breakpoint and up when the phone band has room for fewer chips.
Two to four `outcomes`: the floor sets one column per entry, so it closes the grid; a fifth entry wraps to a second row.
Three `benefits` (or six), each a short `title`, a `description` and an optional `icon`; each renders as a topic with its title as an `h3`.
Four `stats` on the `stats` floor, each a `value` and a `label`, with an optional `prefix` and `suffix`.
Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.
Leave `logo` out of an outcome when the site shows the figure alone; the cell then renders no mark row.
Use `logoTreatment: 'monochrome'` for a dark mark that must invert in the dark theme; leave `color` for a colour mark.
